name: Brazil
sources: World Bank has 1990 GDP at $385bn and 149.1m people, with CPI inflation of 2948% — the year of the Collor Plan. The World Bank's 1990 deposit rate for Brazil is 9394%. Output fell 4.3% over the year (IBGE).

Nothing here scripts that plan: the game opens in January, ten weeks before Collor took office and froze prices and confiscated the savings accounts. What the start state carries is the position he inherited — prices doubling every six weeks, and a nominal rate chasing them. The disinflation is left to the sim's central bank, which is the same treatment Yugoslavia gets.

THE TWO FIGURES ABOVE ARE NOT THE TRANSCRIBED PRINTS. inflation 2.95 is not 2948%; interest_rate 2.9 is not 9394%. The convention everywhere else in this directory is fraction-of-1 (Turkey's 0.603 is 60.3%), so on that convention these would read 29.48 and 93.94. They are stand-ins, and this note exists because the file previously stated the sources above beside numbers that contradicted them.

Why they are stand-ins, measured rather than asserted. Entering 29.48 and 93.94 does not degrade the run, it ends it: Brazil's GDP reaches +inf inside the first simulated year and twelve of the fifty-five tests fail. The cause is in economy.rs — the demand channel is linear and unbounded in the distance of the real rate from neutral, at a coefficient of 0.55 to annual growth, so a real rate of +64 is roughly -3500% annual growth, and 1.0 + growth/12.0 takes GDP through zero every month. Inflation is separately hard-clamped into -0.05..=3.0, so 29.48 would be discarded in month one regardless. Since this commit the loader refuses the corrected pair outright, with the ceiling named.

What the stand-ins are NOT is a designed damping, and the file should not pretend otherwise. Three things say so. First, the scale is a power of ten applied to exactly the three nations whose 1990 percentage needed four digits — Brazil, Poland and Yugoslavia — and to no others; Turkey at 60.3% and Vietnam at 67% are transcribed correctly. That is a decimal shift, not a policy. Second, a damping chosen to preserve the economics would preserve the sign of the real rate: the truth is a policy rate 6400 points above inflation, about as contractionary as a central bank can be, and 2.9 against 2.95 is five points BELOW inflation, which the model reads as easy money. Third, 2.9 is above the ceiling of 0.45 that politics.rs clamps the AI central bank's desired rate to, so the entered rate is transient anyway: it decays with a half-life of about four months and is down to 50% by January 1992.

The cost of the stand-ins, stated so nobody has to rediscover it. On seed 1 Brazil grows 13.9% through 1990 and reaches $530bn by the end of 1991, against an actual contraction of 4.3% followed by roughly flat. The sign of Brazil's early nineties is wrong, and it is wrong because of the real rate these two numbers imply, not because of anything the model does with hyperinflation as such. Fixing it means bounding the real-rate channel in economy.rs; bounding it at +/-0.20 was tried and costs china_growth_miracle (China runs to 17.1x in 30 years) and the trade-integration test, so it is a recalibration and not a one-line change. Until that is done these numbers stay and this note stays with them.
Oil: Petrobras pumped 0.63 mbd from Campos against 1.4 mbd of demand, so Brazil was buying, not selling.
